newsitem.title: USA: Shell Oil Co chemicals boosted Q2.
newsitem.headline: Shell Oil Co chemicals boosted Q2.

text.p: Shell Oil Co, U.S. subsidiary of Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said that adjusted net income for its chemical operations rose $82 million to $155 million in the second quarter of 1997 from a year ago.
This helped the company to offset flat refining margins and a decline in income from its exploration and production units to post a seven percent rise in adjusted net income to $476 million.
Total second quarter net income rose 15 percent to $531 million.
Revenues were $7.09 billion, down from $7.2 billion a year ago. Refined products revenues were $3.65 billion against $3.57 billion a year ago.
Shell said that refining and marketing net income excluding special items fell $19 to million to $129 million.
Total refinery processing intakes were 1.06 million barrels per day (bpd), up from 953,0000 bpd.
Crude oil price declines, to $16.43 from $18.02 per barrel in the U.S. and to $16.94 from $18.43 internationally caused crude revenues to slip to $1.47 billion from $1.79 billion.
The decline was exacerbated by a fall in U.S. crude production to 320,000 barrels per day from 374,000 and flat international output at 49,000 barrels per day.
Natural gas prices were also down, at $2.10 from $2.37 and production fell to 1.66 billion cubic feet per day from 1.9 billion and revenues slid to $463 million from $592 million.
Adjusted net income for oil and gas exploration was $252 million, down from $280 million, while income from continuing operations was $262 million versus $307 million.

Shell's capital and exploration spending fell to $907 million from $1.0 billion, due largely to $124 million fall in chemical investment to $83 million and a $33 million fall in investment in oil products.
Shell is in the process of forming a refining and marketing joint venture will Texaco Inc and Saudi Aramco in the U.S. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
